records.title: Get out and vote in General Election
records.description: Make sure you know what’s on the ballot before you vote in the 2026 General Election Tuesday, Nov. 3. From the top, U.S. Sen. Mike Rounds’ seat is up for a six-year term. Rounds, a Republican, is opposed by Independent candidate Brian L. Bengs. For U.S. Representative, Republican candidate Marty Jackley will face Democratic candidate Nicole “Nikki” Gronli for the two-year seat vacated by Dusty Johnson.

records.title: Merchants Trick-or-Treat Friday
records.description: The annual Merchants’ Trick-or-Treat is taking place in downtown Custer from 4-6 p.m. this Friday, Oct. 30. Community members are encouraged to dress up in their favorite costumes and enjoy a night full of trick-or-treating fun, treats, community and Halloween cheers.

records.title: City answers access questions
records.description: Custer County had questions. The City of Custer had answers. Questions and concerns raised at the Oct. 7 meeting of the Custer County Commission regarding access to Granite Heights Road for future residents planned multi-family housing at the Bearded Buffalo Resort were assuaged at the commission’s Oct. 21 meeting, as Trent Bruce of DGR Engineering, acting on behalf of the city, told commissioners of solutions and preparations already made for the housing.

records.title: Power transfers back to original board
records.description: After changing the locks three times in 10 days, the Custer Senior Center is back under the direction of the originally elected board members as of Oct. 19. This board includes Betty Sowder (president), Roberta Duncan, Tony Gonsor, Shirley Lake, Vickie Hanson and Al Krienke and will be referred to as board one for this story’s purposes. Another board was appointed by members of the Custer Senior Center at an unofficial emergency meeting Oct. 9 when members called for the dismissal of board one by a 33-5 vote. This group will be referred to as board two.

records.title: Housing project ready to launch
records.description: In order to attend the Homecoming Coronation ceremony Oct. 12, the Custer School District Board of Education moved its regularly scheduled meeting from Hermosa to Custer and breezed through a short agenda. The facilities and transportation committee met with the contractors who are going to be involved with the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Community Housing Project.

Veterans Day celebrations
records.description: Custer County is getting ready to honor veterans for their service with events Nov. 11 and 12. Starting in late October, Hometown Hero banners were hung on light poles around the City of Custer. The banners individually recognize veterans with photos in uniform and brief descriptions of their service.

records.title: County upgrades cybersecurity
records.description: Custer County is adding a new layer of cybersecurity to its technology infrastructure, all in the name of avoiding the kind of cyber attack that crippled Pennington County not long ago.

records.title: Project phases winding down for city
records.description: Progress was the theme of the Oct. 19 meeting of the Custer City Council, as the council OK’d a pair of notices of substantial completion of a pair of projects with the city, including West Dam.

records.title: Buffalo Auction is Saturday
records.description: The 61st Annual Custer State Park Fall Classic Bison Auction is scheduled for this Saturday, Nov. 7, at 10 a.m. When it rolls around, the park will be selling more animals than it has in recent years due to drought conditions.

records.title: City council OKs additional FD funding
records.description: The Custer Volunteer Fire Department will receive $269,500 in additional funding from the City of Custer in 2026, this after the Custer City Council approved the allocation of the additional funding at its Nov. 2 meeting. The deparment intially requested the addtional funding at the council’s July 20 meeting, but at that time department chief Matt Spring was told the council wanted more information about the department’s proposed budget.

records.title: Voter turnout was record low
records.description: “This year’s general election saw the lowest voter turnout in the state in more than 50 years,” wrote Molly Wetsch with South Dakota News Watch in her article “General election: SD voter turnout hits historic low, sales tax increases fail.” In the 2022 midterm election, nearly 60 percent of registered voters headed to the polls, according to Wetsch.

records.title: Buffalo auction sets record
records.description: It was a big day for Custer State Park last Saturday, Nov. 7, as the park sold 579 bison for a total of $1,577,000 at its 61st annual bison auction. Both the number of bison sold and the total sales set records for the park’s auction, according to park visitor services supervisor Lydia Austin. Austin said there were 66 bidders from 17 states participating online and in person.

records.title: Concerns raised over court merger
records.description: The South Dakota Supreme Court heard concerns Monday at the Capitol in Pierre from people who said the proposed merger of two western judicial circuits could leave rural communities behind. The proposal would combine the state’s 4th and 7th Judicial Circuits into a single 12-county 4th Circuit headquartered in Rapid City, reducing the number of judicial circuits in South Dakota from seven to six. The 4th Judicial Circuit encompasses the northwestern part of the state, including Butte, Corson, Dewey, Harding, Lawrence, Meade, Perkins and Ziebach counties.

records.description: Just recently in Custer, a man inadvertently started a fire by breaking a burner phone in half and throwing it in a trash can. Strange, yes. The full story? As Seth Thompson will tell you, “You can’t make this s*** up.” The man apparently had the phone so that he could view—let’s say, adult-themed material—without his wife knowing. He began to feel remorse for this, so he threw the phone away.

records.title: Thank a veteran for their service
records.description: Hundreds of veterans, students and community members gathered in the Custer Armory Nov. 11 for the 32nd annual Veterans Day Program presented by the Custer Jr./Sr. High School Student Council and the American Legion Post No. 46.

records.title: School board talks bonuses
records.description: Sleigh bells will soon be ringing, and Custer School District (CSD) employees will find an extra gift in their stocking this holiday season. The best way to go about this was discussed at the board of education meeting Nov. 9 at Hermosa School. Superintendent of Schools Dr. Tim Frederick informed the board that district bonuses have been $100 for the last three years, offered respectively in the form of Custer Cash and $25 gift cards to four Hermosa businesses.

records.title: Leadership change at The Storehouse
records.description: For the first time since its inception, The Storehouse has a new director. Jill Hohn became the facility’s second director toward the end of October, replacing the retiring Kim Canete, although Canete will stay on through the end of the year to help with Hohn’s transition into the role. Hohn said like many people, she knew about The Storehouse but didn’t know about the intricacies involved there. She was on Facebook when she saw the advertisement for the position, and decided it would be something she would like to do.

records.title: Shop local on Pink Friday Nov. 20
records.description: The Custer Area Chamber of Commerce wants you to get ready to kick off the holiday shopping season by showing some love to the locally owned businesses that make Custer so special. Friday, Nov. 20, is for Pink Friday—before the big Black Friday shopping rush, the chamber wants you to make a point to shop small, support local and keep holiday dollars right here in our community. “And this year, we’re making shopping local even more fun with Custer’s Pink Friday Shopping Passport,” chamber director Dawn Murray said.

records.title: Benefit for Ron Tietsort Dec. 4
records.description: Join the community in supporting a local family Friday, Dec. 4 at the State Game Lodge Event Barn in Custer State Park from 5-8 p.m. Life changed drastically for Ron and Jen Tietsort when Ron experienced a sudden medical emergency on a fishing trip in Wayne, Neb., at the end of October. Ron was admitted to the emergency room in Wayne and was then flown to Rapid City.

records.title: Holly jolly Christmas lineup for Custer County
records.description: O come, all ye faithful, the Custer community is coming together to deck the halls with boughs of holly and wish everyone a merry Christmas. Kicking off the holiday season, Custer County Candy Co., is hosting a special visit from Santa Claus from 1-2 p.m. during its open house Saturday, Nov. 28, from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. Enjoy Small Business Saturday with treats, door prizes, hot cocoa and more.

records.title: Physical dam, spillway construction complete
records.description: The earth has been moved, the sediment removed and the concrete poured. You’re up, Mother Nature. It was right around two years ago to the day the Custer  City Council unanimously approved going out for bids to breach West Dam, have the creek diverted and a storm water pollution prevention plan formed—the first steps in renovating and rebuilding the dam, which had sat broken with an empty reservoir since 2012.

records.title: Finishing touches put on phase three
records.description: The Custer City Council at its Nov. 16 meeting voted to approve a change order to put some of the finishing touches on the third phase of the West Dam project. The council voted to add $8,722 to the project to furnish and install public access improvements in the form of signs and gates to be mounted to the auxiliary spillway to warn and protect the public from entry during periods when water is flowing over the spillway. Signs will be posted at the spillway stilling basin, primary intake area and spillway crest to warn the public of potential fall areas, as well.
